control.observation: The clock fills the pane and the three phrases are easy to scan. Choosing an option sends it immediately.
control.accessibility: Three named buttons report their pressed state. The clock has no accessible description of its hands.
control.alt: A large analogue clock above three time phrases.

sdk.observation: The options are easy to scan. A radio selection can be changed before Skicka.
sdk.accessibility: The question names the radio group and arrow keys change the checked option. The clock still has no accessible description of its hands.
sdk.alt: An analogue clock with three radio options and a send button.

control.observation: Short explanations cue each stage. The fixed list makes the learner type out the sequence.
control.accessibility: The list, text field, and send button have usable semantics. There are no move controls.
control.alt: Four mixed water-cycle stages with short descriptions and a text answer field.

sdk.observation: The stage descriptions are still present. Moving each card is easier than transcribing four labels.
sdk.accessibility: The list and move controls have names. A live region gives the item's new position and keyboard focus stays with the moved row.
sdk.alt: Four water-cycle stage cards with up and down buttons.

control.observation: The learner has to translate their choices into a typed code. The example in the answer label gives away the first pair. The shell flags the text as slightly dense.
control.accessibility: The lists are exposed as paragraphs. The answer field and send button have names.
control.alt: Numbered English phrases above lettered meanings, followed by a text field.

sdk.observation: Each English phrase has its own picker. The learner works directly with the meanings and the page gives away no pair.
sdk.accessibility: The pickers have distinct names and the keyboard can submit a complete map. The English phrases lack a language tag.
sdk.alt: Three English café phrases with one meaning picker per phrase.

control.observation: The events are mixed, the direction is clear, and the learner needs to type names or invent shorthand in a single field.
control.accessibility: The list, text field, and send button have usable semantics. There are no move controls.
control.alt: Four mixed events in Swedish parliamentary history and an answer field.

sdk.observation: The learner can move long event names directly. The instructions repeat, and the starting order is one swap from the answer.
sdk.accessibility: The list exposes each event and its move controls. A move updates the live position and keeps focus on the item.
sdk.alt: Four Swedish parliamentary events with up and down buttons.

control.observation: The scale and short hint support the question, and the answer field leaves the operation to the learner.
control.accessibility: The answer field and send button have names. The equation heading and scale are unnamed in the accessibility tree.
control.alt: An equation placed on two pans of a scale, followed by a short answer field.

sdk.observation: The scale and answer field fit. The hint says minus, which gives away the operation, and the question names only the left side of the scale.
sdk.accessibility: The response field is named. The equation heading and scale still lack accessible text.
sdk.alt: An equation scale and a text field with the placeholder t.ex. minus.

control.observation: The hint distinguishes quantity from unit and gives a word bank. Each gap submits when focus leaves it, with little indication of when an answer is sent.
control.accessibility: All three text fields share the generic accessible name Lucka.
control.alt: Three fill-in-the-blank electrical quantities and a word bank of units.

sdk.observation: The short distinction between quantity and unit sets up the exercise. Each quantity has a picker and Skicka sends one complete answer.
sdk.accessibility: Three differently named pickers replace the three identical gap labels.
sdk.alt: Three electrical quantities, each with a unit picker.

summary: Four of six exercises were clearer with the new blocks. Ordering and matching benefited most. Keep testing the blocks before adopting the SDK dependency.
bundle: The prototype inlines a 223,793-byte UI SDK bundle into experiment frames (79,656 bytes gzip). The web app entry chunk grew by 245,670 raw bytes and 84,020 gzip bytes.
